pages.title: The best budget laptops under $800 in 2026
pages.content: We tested eleven machines under $800 over six weeks. Three are worth your money. The Aveo Zen 14 ($749) is the all-round pick: a bright 14-inch panel, a keyboard that survives long typing sessions, and eleven hours of real battery life. The Kestrel Pro 15 ($799) trades battery for a faster chip and a larger screen, which suits anyone compiling or editing video. The Nimbus Air 13 ($679) is the cheapest we can recommend, though the display is dimmer than both. Full reviews: https://techroundup.example.com/reviews/aveo-zen-14 and https://techroundup.example.com/reviews/kestrel-pro-15 and https://techroundup.example.com/reviews/nimbus-air-13.

pages.title: Aveo Zen 14 review: the sensible budget pick
pages.content: The Aveo Zen 14 costs $749. Strengths: 11 hours of measured battery life, a 400-nit display, 16GB of memory soldered but adequate, and a chassis that does not flex. Weaknesses: the integrated graphics are slow under sustained load, the webcam is poor, and there is one USB-C port too few. Sustained multi-core performance is roughly 20 percent behind the Kestrel Pro 15, which matters if you compile often. For general study and office work it is the better daily machine of the two.

pages.title: Kestrel Pro 15 review: more speed, less endurance
pages.content: The Kestrel Pro 15 costs $799. Strengths: the fastest sustained multi-core performance in this price band, a 15.6-inch 500-nit screen, upgradeable memory, and two full-speed USB-C ports. Weaknesses: 6.5 hours of measured battery life, an audible fan under load, and 2.1kg of weight. Against the Aveo Zen 14 the trade is straightforward: you gain roughly 20 percent sustained CPU throughput and lose about four hours away from a charger.

pages.title: Laptop CPU benchmarks, 2026 mid-range roundup
pages.content: Sustained multi-core scores after a 20-minute load, higher is better. Kestrel Pro 15: 8,940. Aveo Zen 14: 7,410. Nimbus Air 13: 6,120. Single-core results are within five percent of each other across all three, so the gap is a cooling story rather than a silicon one. Thermal throttling begins at eight minutes on the Nimbus Air 13 and not at all on the Kestrel Pro 15.

pages.title: Measured battery life: 2026 budget laptops
pages.content: All figures are from a looped web-browsing test at 150 nits. Aveo Zen 14: 11 hours 10 minutes. Nimbus Air 13: 9 hours 5 minutes. Kestrel Pro 15: 6 hours 30 minutes. Charging to 80 percent takes 55 minutes on the Aveo and 40 minutes on the Kestrel, which partly offsets the endurance difference for people who work near an outlet.

pages.title: Nimbus Air 13 review: cheap, light, dim
pages.content: The Nimbus Air 13 costs $679 and weighs 1.2kg. It is the lightest machine here and the only one with a fanless design. The display peaks at 250 nits, which is workable indoors and frustrating near a window. Performance is adequate for documents and browsing but throttles under sustained load. Buy it for portability and price, not for speed.

pages.title: Laptop reliability survey: two-year failure rates
pages.content: Survey of 4,200 owners reporting hardware failures within 24 months of purchase. Aveo: 6.1 percent. Kestrel: 7.4 percent. Nimbus: 9.8 percent. Hinge and battery-swell complaints dominate the Nimbus figure. Warranty service satisfaction was highest for Aveo and lowest for Nimbus.

pages.title: How to pick a laptop without overpaying
pages.content: Decide the three things you actually need before reading any review. Screen brightness under 300 nits is a daily annoyance. Sixteen gigabytes of memory is the floor if the machine cannot be upgraded later. Battery claims from manufacturers are measured at low brightness and should be discounted by roughly a third. Ports matter more than thinness for most people.

pages.title: Back-to-school laptop deals this week
pages.content: Current listings under $800: Aveo Zen 14 at $749, Kestrel Pro 15 at $799, Nimbus Air 13 at $649 after an instant discount. Stock on the Nimbus is limited to selected regions. Prices update daily and student verification adds a further five percent on the Aveo.

pages.title: Laptop - OpenWiki
pages.content: A laptop is a portable personal computer with a clamshell form factor, combining the display, keyboard, pointing device, and battery in a single unit. Design trade-offs centre on thermal capacity, battery mass, and screen size, which together determine sustained performance and endurance. See also: ultrabook, mobile workstation, thermal design power.

pages.title: Vortex Slim 12 review: a competent new arrival under $800
pages.content: The Vortex Slim 12 costs $739. Strengths: a rigid aluminium lid, a quiet fan curve, 16GB of memory, and a 512GB drive at a price that undercuts most of the segment. Weaknesses: measured battery life is 6.5 hours on the same looped browsing test where the Aveo Zen 14 reaches 11, the display peaks at 300 nits so it washes out near a window, and sustained multi-core performance sits behind both the Kestrel Pro 15 and the Aveo. It is a reasonable machine at the price and a poor choice if battery life or screen brightness matter to you.
